extracted.intended_audience: aspiring authors seeking literary agents / authors preparing query letters
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing query letters to attract literary agents and prompt requests for manuscripts and offers of representation; includes format, length, hook, and where to get critique or agent contacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose & definition of a book query letter
rubrics_metrics.description: What is a book query letter?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the query letter to get a literary agent to request and read your manuscript; it is the instrument that connects a talented author with the right person at an agency or publishing house.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optimal length for a query letter
rubrics_metrics.description: What’s the best length for a query letter?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep length in mind as a key criterion (the site promises guidance on the best length); concision is implied as important so agents will read to the end.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between query letter and book synopsis
rubrics_metrics.description: What’s the difference between an agent query letter and a book synopsis?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand that a query letter is not the same as a synopsis and that each has a different purpose and expected content when submitting to agents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Query letter format (popular formats)
rubrics_metrics.description: What’s the most popular query letter format?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow a commonly accepted format/structure for queries (the site provides guidance on which formats are most used); format choices affect readability and professionalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability and use of sample query letters and templates
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there a sample book query letter, book query letter example, or query letter template I can model?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sample letters and templates as models to structure and tone your own query; the site offers examples and a 15-part training to study model queries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hook — craft an effective opening
rubrics_metrics.description: What’s an agent query letter hook—and what’s the best one to use?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A strong hook is a central criterion: craft an opening that compels the agent to keep reading; the site promises instruction on what makes the best hooks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include SASE for mailed submissions when required
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Know submission-related procedural requirements such as including a self-addressed stamped envelope (SASE) for postal queries when agents request materials by mail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate format for email vs. mailed queries
rubrics_metrics.description: What is the best book query letter format and email query letter format?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adapt your query to the medium—follow conventions for both physical (mailed) and electronic (email) query formats; the site provides separate guidance for each.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluating and selecting which advice to follow
rubrics_metrics.description: How can I tell which advice about query letters to follow—and ignore?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vet sources of query-letter advice; the site aims to separate good advice from bad and explain why insiders disagree, so prioritize guidance from experienced agents and reputable coaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Getting a professional critique
rubrics_metrics.description: Where can I get a query letter critique?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek external critique services or coaching to refine your query; the site offers information on critique options and connections to author coaching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeting the right agent / recipient research
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the right person at a literary agency or publishing house to read your work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research agents and target submissions appropriately so the right agent (one who handles your genre and is open to submissions) receives your letter; the site provides a Directory of Literary Agents for this purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim for measurable results (requests, offers, publisher interest)
rubrics_metrics.description: Write your query letter so literary agents will read your book and generate manuscript requests, representation offers, and publisher interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ultimate metric of a successful query is agent engagement resulting in requests or offers; craft queries with the goal of producing those outcomes (the site’s training is positioned to increase requests and offers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of author credentials and credibility signals
rubrics_metrics.description: Include relevant author biography, publishing credits, awards, or professional credentials to build credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate why you are qualified to write this book (the author’s own bio is used as an example of building credibility); include concise, pertinent credentials in the query when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of curated resources (agent directories and resource library)
rubrics_metrics.description: Utilize directories and resource libraries to find agents and learn submission practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage the provided Directory of Literary Agents and Author Resource Library to research agents, learn about submission mechanics, and access topic-specific guidance (e.g., how to get a fiction agent, how to submit after self-publishing).
